_activity: Build the explanation: the three-fifths clause
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the 11.2 casefile documents (numbered per the signed 11.2 map). Quotes are the casefile's adapted text.
intro: Build the sentence. Drag the correct piece into each blank.

tiles.text: The three-fifths clause counted enslaved people toward a state's seats in the House
The Senate gave each state two senators
The Articles gave each state one vote
Southern delegates wanted more seats in Congress
enslaved people were allowed to vote
big states wanted every state counted the same
slaveholding states gained power from people who could not vote
enslaved people gained a voice in Congress

correct_sentence: The three-fifths clause counted enslaved people toward a state's seats in the House, because Southern delegates wanted more seats in Congress, which means slaveholding states gained power from people who could not vote.
rationale: The casefile's Explanation frame, filled from Document 14. The “which means” is the part most answers skip.
hints: Start with the part of Document 14 about counting people.
Who wanted the extra seats, and who paid for them?
